**About Concurrence**
Concurrence (formerly Amigo) is building the platform healthcare organizations use to build their own clinical AI agents. Our mission is to make excellent care accessible to every patient, not rationed by the limits of clinician time.
  
  
Underneath our platform is the Health World Model, which unifies a health system’s data into a living, event-level record of every patient’s care. On top of it, agents handle work across the patient journey, from intake and scheduling to medication management and clinical decision support.
  
  
Our agents have supported more than 10 million patient encounters and are on track to grow tenfold this year. We run natively on Databricks, integrate with every major EHR, and are backed by Madrona, General Catalyst, and Optum Ventures. We’re about 35 people, working in person in New York and San Francisco.
  
  
**About The Role**
Applied AI is where Concurrence meets the real world. Our core engineering team builds the platform. We take it into health systems and build what each customer actually needs on top of it, as durable software that runs in production.
  
  
As a Senior Applied AI Engineer, you own an entire customer use case, not a ticket or a slice of one. You take a deployment from brief to production. You make the architecture calls inside it, commit the timeline, and carry the outcome.
  
  
Success isn't your agent staying up. It's the customer's number moving: more intake handled, fewer denials, faster time to billing close.
  
  
Your work doesn't stop at one customer. We build custom first, on purpose. When the same shape shows up under two customers, you're the one who sees it, and the pattern you proved becomes part of the platform everyone builds on next.
  
  
Applied AI runs ahead of the platform, not behind it. Our field work is the R&D that decides what Concurrence becomes.
  
  
****What you'll do****

* Own a whole use case, end to end. You run the build from the deployment brief to production and beyond. You set its internal design, commit the timelines, and ship at a bar that doesn't need anyone checking behind you.
* Build agent systems that hold up in clinical settings. That means hierarchies of agents and skills rather than one monolith, and evals that measure distributions, not vibes. Nothing reaches a patient until it clears our safety floor and eval gate.
* Take on the integration reality. EHRs, legacy systems, and customer data come in every shape. You find the path from what the customer has to what the platform needs.
* Make it compound. You turn field-proven patterns into first-class platform capabilities. You also push proven work down from agent reasoning into deterministic data lookups, the move where twenty tool calls become one. That's how we grow without turning into a services shop.
* Push back early. When a spec was never vetted, an integration isn't supported, or scope quietly changed mid-build, you raise it before the build pays for it.
* Raise the people around you. Mentor the engineers on your use case and help set how the team builds. Write documentation good enough that a coding agent or a new hire could pick up your work.

****You might be a great fit if you****

* Have shipped and owned complex production systems end to end, with real users depending on them.
* Have real experience building with LLMs and agents in production, or the engineering depth to get there fast.
* Treat non-deterministic systems with rigor. You know three runs of an agent is a feeling, not evidence.
* Hold the near term and the long term at once: what a decision costs now, and what it makes easier or harder for the team later.
* Are comfortable in the room with customers and clinicians. You'd rather understand the workflow than wait for a perfect spec.
* Care about craft. Your systems fail loudly to you before they fail to a customer, and they keep working while you're on vacation.

****Nice to have****

* Healthcare experience: EHR integrations (Epic, Oracle Health, athenahealth), HL7, FHIR, or clinical workflows.
* Experience with Databricks, voice agents, or forward deployed or customer engineering.
* Time at an early-stage startup.

****Why this role****

* Stakes. Your work runs inside health systems and touches patient care.
* Ownership, early. You own whole use cases from the start. At a 35-person company, scope arrives fast.
* Leverage. What you build in the field becomes the platform. Few roles let you shape the product this directly.
* A clear path. Our Applied AI ladder runs from Senior to Staff or Tech Lead. You move up by the kind of work you can be trusted to own, not by how much you ship.
* A week built for deep work. Collaborative in-office sprints early in the week, a protected focus day on Thursday, and Friday to consolidate what we learned.

**Benefits (available to Full-Time Employees)**
**Health & Wellness**

* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
* Daily catered lunch and dinner
* Mental health support and wellness coaching
* Flexible wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or personal growth

**Growth & Development**

* Annual learning budget for courses, books, or conferences
* Conference attendance budget for professional development
* Annual team offsite
* Academic collaboration opportunities
* Unlimited PTO

**Our Core Values**

* Patients Win, We Win

If patients aren't getting better care, we haven't earned the right to scale. Every internal decision gets pressure-tested: does this make patients' lives better? If we can't draw the line, we question why we're doing it.
  
  

* High Standards, High Care

We hold a high bar for the team because patients are counting on us to get this right. But high standards only work with genuine investment in each other. You can take risks, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas. Not despite our standards, but because of them.
  
  

* Thoughtful Urgency

We move fast by default, but speed without judgment is recklessness. The discipline is knowing which decisions are reversible vs. not. In healthcare AI, the companies that win will be fast everywhere they can be and careful everywhere they must be. We build the muscle to do both.
  
  

* Intensely Measured

We instrument patient outcomes, provider ROI, system performance, and clinical accuracy. But data without action is surveillance. Every metric should have an owner, a threshold, and a response plan. If we're measuring something but never acting on it, we stop measuring it.
**Who Builds With Us**

* Low ego: Politics and territory don't interest you. The best ideas win, regardless of who has them.
* Direct: You say the hard thing, challenge ideas openly, and commit fully once decided.
* High agency: You thrive on trust rather than instruction. When you see something is broken, you fix it. You don’t file tickets and wait for someone else.
* Bar of excellence: You hold yourself to a bar most people wouldn't, and you want teammates who do the same.
* Skeptical: You push back on rules that don’t make sense and question assumptions that haven’t earned their place.

Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

**Description**
At Commence, we’re the start of a new age of data-centric transformation, elevating health outcomes and powering better, more efficient process to program and patient health. We combine quality data-driven solutions that fuel answers, technology that advances performance, and clinical expertise that builds trust to create a more efficient path to quality care.
  
  
With human-centered, healthcare-relevant, and value-based solutions, we create new possibilities with data. We provide proof beyond the concept and performance beyond the scope with a focus on efficiencies that transform the lives of those we serve. With a culture driven by purpose, straightforward communication and clinical domain expertise, Commence cuts straight to better care.?
  
  
**Requirements**
The AI/ML Engineer builds, trains, and validates machine learning models that power clinical and operational data products across the healthcare ecosystem, and contributes hands-on to productionizing those models, including supporting document processing pipelines and AI/LLM-driven workflows.
  
  
The ideal candidate has solid hands-on ML experience, is comfortable working with healthcare datasets (EHRs, claims, FHIR), and can independently own well-scoped model development work while relying on senior engineers for system design, compliance, and architecture decisions.
  
  

* Build, train, and validate machine learning models, including data ingestion, feature engineering, and model evaluation, against requirements defined by Senior Engineers or Data Scientists.
* Contribute to productionizing machine learning and AI models into APIs, batch, and streaming workflows, under the direction of Senior AI/ML Engineers.
* Support development of AI/LLM-driven workflows (e.g., document extraction, classification, summarization) using frameworks and orchestration patterns established by senior technical staff.
* Assist in implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) components, embedding strategies, and vector-based retrieval within architecture designed by senior engineers.
* Apply established MLOps practices, including CI/CD pipelines, model versioning, and retraining workflows, within existing team standards.
* Work within Databricks (Workflows, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog) and AWS services (S3, Lambda, Bedrock) to support model training and inference tasks.
* Monitor deployed model performance (latency, throughput, accuracy drift) and troubleshoot issues, escalating architecture-level problems to Senior Engineers.
* Use and maintain existing monitoring, alerting, and observability tooling for models the engineer owns.
* Collaborate with Data Engineers, Data Scientists, and Software Engineers to deliver assigned components of larger AI/ML systems.
* Follow established practices to keep AI/ML work compliant with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, FedRAMP Moderate, and other applicable regulatory frameworks.
* Implement secure data handling practices, including encryption, access controls, and protection of sensitive healthcare data.
* Stay current on emerging AI/ML tools and techniques and bring relevant options to the team for evaluation.
* Document model development, testing, and validation work to support reproducibility and audit readiness.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field.
* 3-5 years of experience in machine learning engineering, data science, or software engineering.
* Strong proficiency in programming languages such as Python and SQL, with experience building production-grade systems.
* Practical experience with ML libraries such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
* Experience deploying machine learning models to production environments (batch or API-based), with support from senior engineers on system design.
* Exposure to AI/LLM platforms such as AWS Bedrock, Anthropic, LangChain, or Databricks Agent frameworks.
* Familiarity with distributed data processing frameworks such as PySpark, Databricks, or AWS EMR.
* Experience with ML lifecycle tools such as MLflow, model registries, and monitoring frameworks.
* Experience building APIs or services (e.g., FastAPI, Flask) for model inference.
* Solid understanding of software engineering principles and their application to ML workflows.
* Experience working with healthcare datasets such as EHRs, claims, FHIR, or HL7.
* Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills across technical and non-technical teams.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Exposure to vector databases, embeddings, or RAG components.
* Experience with OCR/document AI tools (e.g., AWS Textract, DBX OCR).
* Experience with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes).
* Familiarity with healthcare data governance and security frameworks such as NIST or HITRUST.
* Experience supporting federal healthcare programs or agencies such as CMS, VA, or DoD.
* Knowledge of healthcare delivery systems, quality measurement programs, or policy frameworks.

**About Us**
At Armadin, we're a group of engineers, researchers, and security researchers on a mission to redefine what proactive security can do in the AI era. Cyberattacks are becoming autonomous and relentless and we believe defending against threats before they materialize is one of the most powerful ways to protect the institutions the world depends on.
  
  
We're building autonomous proactive security from the ground up, reinforcing the tradecraft of elite security practioners into purpose-built security models and agents that discover risk and remediate it before organizations are breached.
  
  
Led by Kevin Mandia, founder of Mandiant ($5.4B exit to Google), our team brings together researchers and engineers from Google, xAI, Meta, Stanford, Georgia Tech, Waterloo, Berkeley, and MIT to reinvent security for an adversary that never sleeps.
  
  
The Role
  
  
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Armadin, you'll embed with enterprise teams, deploy our agentic platform into their environment, and build whatever it takes to make it work for them. You're the person in the room when the customer hits a wall and the person who ships the fix that night. Your job is to make every customer feel like Armadin was built for them, then bring what you learn back into the product so the next deployment is faster than the last.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Deliver the Magic: Own the customer journey from pre-sales scoping through deployment and expansion, making the first weeks feel effortless.
* Customize at the Edge: Build customer-specific integrations, workflows, and agent configurations on top of the Armadin platform.
* Embed with Customers: Work directly with security, platform, and DevOps teams and CISOs, turning ambiguous requirements and compliance constraints into shipped deployment plans.
* Build the Playbook: Turn what you do by hand into runbooks, automation, and self-service tooling for every customer after.
* Close the Loop with Product: Bring field signal back to Engineering, Product, and Research.
* Own Operational Health: Lead upgrades, scaling, and incident support for our most critical deployments.

What You'll Bring
  
  

* Forward Deployed DNA: You've worked as a forward deployed engineer, deployment strategist, solutions engineer, or similar, and have a track record of owning customer outcomes in the field.
* Top-Tier AI Experience: Time at a leading AI company or AI-native startup where you shipped LLM-powered products to real customers.
* Technical Range: Strong software fundamentals plus hands-on cloud and deployment depth (AWS, Terraform, containers, networking), including deployments into customer-owned environments.
* Bias to Ship: You'd rather build a working solution on-site than write a requirements doc, and you own what you build through operational health.
* AI Fluency & Judgment: AI shapes how you build, and you know when to configure, when to extend, and when to push a capability back into the core platform.
* Degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Even Better With
  
  

* Early-stage experience building deployment operations, playbooks, and tooling from scratch.
* Go, Python, or TypeScript services in production.

**About Corgi**

Corgi is a full-stack insurance carrier building better, faster insurance products for startups. We’re not a broker, so we underwrite and issue policies directly, with fewer handoffs and less friction. Cutting out intermediaries lets us tailor coverage to how companies actually operate and price risk more efficiently.

We build insurance products from the ground up, using AI and software to automate the workflows traditionally handled by large teams of brokers, underwriters, TPAs, accountants, and operations staff. Our goal is not to incrementally improve insurance, it is to rebuild the industry infrastructure itself.

We move quickly, care deeply about talent density, and hire people who want to solve difficult problems with unusually high ownership.

**About the Role**

We're hiring an Applied AI Engineer to build and deploy AI systems that power our insurance companies and internal operations.

You will work closely with engineering, product, operations, and leadership to develop AI-powered products and automate complex workflows across underwriting, claims, finance, compliance, and internal tooling. This is a highly hands-on role for someone who enjoys experimenting with emerging AI technologies, shipping quickly, and turning cutting-edge models into reliable production systems.

**What You'll Do**

* Build and deploy AI-powered applications, agents, and automation systems.
* Design and implement LLM-based workflows across underwriting, claims, finance, and internal operations.
* Develop AI systems that can reason over documents, extract structured information, and execute complex tasks.
* Experiment with foundation models, fine-tuning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic architectures.
* Build evaluation frameworks to measure model accuracy, reliability, latency, and performance.
* Integrate AI capabilities into existing software systems, APIs, and internal tools.
* Work closely with domain experts to identify opportunities to replace manual processes with AI-driven workflows.
* Improve the scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency of production AI systems.
* Stay at the forefront of AI research and translate emerging capabilities into real products.

**Who You Are**

* Strong software engineering fundamentals with a deep interest in AI and machine learning.
* Comfortable building with LLMs, experimenting with new models, and deploying AI systems into production.
* Curious about how AI can fundamentally transform traditional industries.
* Comfortable working in ambiguity, iterating quickly, and solving open-ended technical problems.
* High ownership and bias toward execution.
* Excited to work closely with operators, engineers, and domain experts.
* Motivated by building AI systems that have measurable real-world impact.

**Preferred Experience**

* 3+ years of software engineering, machine learning, or applied AI experience.
* Strong proficiency in Python and experience with modern AI/ML frameworks.

**Description**
Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing and most profitable businesses, responsible for defining and delivering AI-powered solutions that transform how advertisers make strategic decisions. We deliver billions of ad impressions and process massive volumes of advertiser data every single day. You'll work with us to pioneer breakthrough approaches in how AI agents access and reason over real-time advertiser data at scale.
  
  
The Campaign Management team is responsible for capturing inputs for advertisers to control their advertising efforts. You can think of our team as the brain and nervous system of all the advertisements you see on amazon.com. We build large scale, high velocity distributed systems to service 100’s of millions of API requests per day, steam data at PB scale, process business logic on tight latency budgets, all while streaming and the data at high fidelity to 20+ other services to perform other critical advertising functions. We stand up world class CI/CD pipelines to deploy our service automating infrastructure provisioning, high volume load testing and first-rate monitoring so our engineers can keep their heads down inventing for our advertisers. Our problem space covers concurrent workflows across distributed systems (linearizability, eventual consistency), big data problems (propagation delay, ordering and hygiene) and performance (search optimization). Our team uses the latest AWS products and services to solve our problems including but not limited to: ECS, Fargate, EC2, EMR, Lambda, Kafka, Elastic Search, Dynamo DB, SQS, SNS, Cloud watch, CDK, Cloud Formation and many more.
  
  
We are using generative AI and agentic systems to help advertising agents provide instant, strategic advice to millions of advertisers. You will need to invent new techniques for global ads experience, agent orchestration, and context optimization to ensure we're delivering accurate, trustworthy insights with minimal latency and token consumption. You'll create feedback loops to ensure our solutions are constantly evaluating themselves and improving.
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  

* Design and implement scalable architectures for APIs serving millions of advertisers at thousands of transactions per second
* Build Model Context Protocol (MCP) server infrastructure—an emerging standard for AI agent-data interaction—that delivers advertiser context with sub-second latency and minimal token consumption
* Establish system design patterns and best practices for global ads experience at scale

**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

**About Us**
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
  
  
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
  
  
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
  
  
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
  
  
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
  
  
****The Job****
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
  
  
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
  
  
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
  
  
**About You**

At Realtor.com®, we help people discover and create their perfect home. We bring together real estate data, consumer experiences and technology to support people throughout their home journey.
  
  
Realtor.com is building a Customer Data Platform on Twilio Segment so we can recognize consumers across web, apps, email and push and give each person an experience that fits where they are in their home search. It’s heading to production now, and we need engineers to help build and run it.
  
  
We’re hiring a Software Engineer for the CDP’s serving path: the profile store and the Personalization Activation Subgraph, a federated GraphQL service between the CDP and our site and apps. Personalization has to be fast and safe. If anything is slow or down, users and search engines just get the standard page.
  
  
The work is backend-first but goes all the way to the screen. You’ll write resolvers and profile store code, wire the subgraph into our server-rendered pages and CMS, and build the components that render each treatment, its fallback and its exposure events. Over time you’ll own treatments end to end, from the CDP trait to the pixel on the page. You’ll start alongside a senior engineer and our vendor, then help bring the platform in-house with data engineering, Identity & Authentication, Web Platform, Mobile, Notifications and MarTech.
  
  
**Top Reasons To Apply**

* Help build a new platform with real executive sponsorship.
* Work on a system that sits at the meeting point of identity, data and the consumer experience on one of the largest real estate sites in the U.S.
* Grow quickly with senior engineers on work that spans backend, front end and data

**What You’ll Do**

* Build and maintain an Apollo Federation v2 subgraph that serves profile traits, audiences and personalization decisions to web, CMS and native clients, using our schema conventions, resilience patterns (timeouts, circuit breakers, kill switches, flags) and router-provided identity so a CDP failure never breaks a page.
* Help build the RDC-owned profile store and its refresh pipeline (event consumers, backfills, rate-limited batching) to serve traits in single-digit milliseconds, partnering with Web Platform on caching.
* Bring personalization into server-rendered React pages, islands and CMS experiments with Apollo Client components that load without flicker, never block the page and protect Core Web Vitals, with clean exposure and engagement tracking through Segment.
* Help build the Kafka integration that sends identity events to the CDP without PII leakage, and enforce consent and opt-out so suppressed users are never personalized or tracked.
* Ship through EKS, Argo CD, Helm and CircleCI, join on-call once ramped up, build the dashboards, alerts and runbooks for your services, and turn product requirements into flagged, A/B-tested features with short design docs.

**What You’ll Bring**

* 3+ years of software engineering experience, including building and supporting services in production.
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
* Experience shipping user-facing features across both a backend service and the UI.
* Solid TypeScript/Node.js for backend work (our subgraphs are Node/TypeScript).
* React and TypeScript on the front end, with some experience in server-side rendering (Next.js or similar) and a GraphQL client such as Apollo Client.
* Working knowledge of GraphQL APIs: schema design, resolvers and error handling.
* Familiarity with caching and key-value stores (Redis, DynamoDB or similar) and why latency matters for page rendering.
* Understanding of basic resilience patterns: timeouts, retries and fallbacks.
* Experience with AWS, Docker and CI/CD pipelines.
* Habit of writing tests and adding logging and metrics to the code you ship.
* Clear written communication and comfort asking questions and raising risks early.

**Preferred**

* Apollo Federation v2 experience: subgraphs, entities and @key, composition checks with Rover/GraphOS.
* Hands-on work with a Customer Data Platform, ideally Twilio Segment (Engage audiences, computed traits, Profile API, Destinations). mParticle, Tealium, Braze or Amperity also count.
* Kafka or another event streaming system, including idempotency and ordering.
* Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) and front-end performance tuning.
* Feature flag and experimentation tools (LaunchDarkly, Amplitude Experiment, Optimizely) and exposure logging.
* OAuth 2.0/OIDC and JWT basics, or identity platforms like Auth0 or Okta.
* Client-side analytics (Segment analytics.js, Amplitude or similar).
* Kubernetes, Argo CD, Helm and Terraform.
* Observability tools such as New Relic or Datadog.
* Awareness of privacy requirements around PII, consent and opt-out (CCPA/CPRA).
* Micro-frontend, design system or headless CMS experience.

**About Us**
At Thesis, we believe everyone should have the opportunity to meet their potential. We build nootropic supplements and customer experiences that help people find the right support for their goals.
  
  
Across Thesis and Stasis, we're also changing how our company works. Our teams use AI to develop creative, research customers, build digital experiences, analyze performance, and reduce repetitive operational work. We're looking for an engineer who can turn those experiments into reliable systems that people use every day.
  
  
**About The Role**
We're looking for an AI Engineer to build the agents, integrations, and internal tools that help a small team accomplish more. You'll work with Data, Engineering, Growth, Creative, and Operations to find valuable problems, prototype solutions, and own them through deployment, adoption, and ongoing improvement.
  
  
This is a hands-on software engineering role focused on applied AI. You'll build with existing models, connect them to our tools and knowledge, and make their outputs useful and trustworthy. You should be as comfortable debugging an API integration as designing an agent workflow, and care about whether your work saves time, improves decisions, or helps the business grow.
  
  
We already have AI-assisted workflows and a shared Claude skill and knowledge system. You'll build on that foundation, making successful workflows easier to reuse and bringing production engineering to the parts that need it. You won't be starting from a blank page, and you won't be limited to maintaining what's already there.
  
  
How You'll Make an Impact
  
  
Build agents that do useful work
  
  

* Design and ship agents that retrieve information, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks across our business systems.
* Connect workflows across tools such as Slack, Google Workspace, Asana, Shopify, and Klaviyo through APIs, webhooks, and MCP integrations.
* Make long-running workflows dependable with persistent state, retries, duplicate prevention, clear approvals, and recoverable failures.

Accelerate creative and growth workflows
  
  

* Partner with Creative and Growth to improve the path from customer research and performance insights to briefs, scripts, creative variants, and testable landing pages.
* Build workflows that combine brand knowledge, approved product claims, asset libraries, and creative performance data while keeping human review where it matters.
* Help teams learn from prior experiments so each new brief or test benefits from what we've already discovered.

Make company knowledge and data more useful
  
  

* Extend our shared skills, knowledge base, retrieval, and context-management systems so AI tools can find and use the right source material.
* Partner with our data team to connect AI workflows to governed analytics in Metabase and Hex, backed by Snowflake, rather than inventing competing definitions of business metrics.
* Use SQL and data validation to investigate issues, verify outputs, and make analytical workflows easier for non-technical teammates to use.

Turn prototypes into reliable products
  
  

* Build evaluations using real business tasks. Test accuracy, task completion, tool behavior, failure recovery, latency, and cost before scaling a workflow.
* Add monitoring, useful logs, version control, automated tests, and clear documentation. Own failures after launch and fix their causes.
* Protect customer and company data, separate brand and account contexts, and preserve human approval for consequential actions.
* Choose the simplest approach that works, including ordinary code or deterministic automation when an LLM adds no value.

Help the company use AI well
  
  

* Work directly with teammates to understand their workflows, ship usable interfaces, and help them adopt what you build.
* Create reusable skills and integrations rather than isolated prompts that only their author can operate.
* Evaluate new models and tools through practical experiments, then explain what is worth adopting and why.
* Measure outcomes such as time saved, adoption, output quality, and faster experiment cycles, not just the number of automations shipped.

We're Excited About Your
  
  

* Experience shipping software that real users depend on, with ownership beyond the initial prototype.
* Hands-on LLM application development using Anthropic, OpenAI, or comparable APIs, including structured outputs, tool calling, retrieval, and multi-step workflows.
* Strong Python or TypeScript skills, sound software design, and comfort working with APIs, authentication, databases, and asynchronous jobs.
* Practical understanding of RAG, context management, and MCP. You can explain the tradeoffs and show when a simpler approach is better.
* Ability to build evaluations, diagnose unreliable behavior, and improve an AI system using evidence rather than prompt tweaking alone.
* Working SQL proficiency and experience validating data against established reporting or warehouse models.
* Product judgment and clear communication. You can turn an ambiguous request into a focused solution, explain technical tradeoffs, and work effectively with non-technical partners.
* Curiosity, initiative, and follow-through. You experiment independently, learn quickly, and take responsibility for whether your work is useful.

Experience with Claude Code, Codex, shared agent skills, or agent orchestration platforms such as OpenClaw is a plus. So is experience with ecommerce, consumer subscriptions, creative production, multimodal generation, or analytics tools such as PostHog and Metabase. We don't expect you to have used every tool in our stack.
  
  
How You'll Work
  
  
You'll work on problems with visible business impact, from reducing manual reporting to making creative production and customer research more effective. You'll partner closely with the people doing the work, test with real inputs, and keep improving the system after it ships.
  
  
We value people who can move quickly without confusing a convincing demo with a dependable product. Bring strong engineering fundamentals, good judgment about where AI helps, and a willingness to get into the details.

 The Payments and Fraud Data Platform team within AWS Payments \& Fraud is the backbone of one of the most critical missions at AWS: ensuring every transaction is safe, every suspension is justified, and every customer experience is seamless. We process petabytes of data daily, powering the ML models, rule engines, and real\-time reporting systems that allow us to detect bad actors.
   

  

 We are looking for a Software Development Engineer who is passionate about building large\-scale data systems, thrives in ambiguity, and wants to work at the intersection of big data, machine learning, non\-payment and fraud prevention.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

 Architect \& Build Petabyte\-Scale Data Pipelines \- Design, develop, and optimize batch and near\-real\-time data pipelines using Amazon Managed Airflow (MWAA), Fargate, EMR, Apache Iceberg, and Amazon Redshift to ingest, transform, and serve data at massive scale.
   

  

 Power ML \& Rules Engines \- Deliver high\-quality, timely datasets that fuel non payment and fraud detection ML models and business rule engines, directly impacting fraud prevention and non\-payment suspension accuracy.
   

  

 Build Intelligent Data Access Layers \- Design and implement a Smart Query \& Data Access Analyzer that profiles query patterns, identifies hot data, and automatically promotes frequently accessed datasets into hot memory tiers (e.g., OpenSearch, DynamoDB DAX, Redshift RA3 caching) for sub\-second retrieval.
   

  

 Create Natural Language SQL Interfaces \- Leverage Amazon Bedrock and LLM (large language models) to build a natural language\-to\-SQL generation tool that empowers analysts and stakeholders to query complex fraud datasets conversationally \- no SQL expertise required.
   

  

 Develop Real\-Time Dashboards \& Insights \- Build rich, interactive dashboards using Grafana and internal tooling that provide real\-time visibility into fraud trends, pipeline health, data quality metrics, and operational KPIs.
   

  

 Curate a Living Data Dictionary \- Design and maintain a comprehensive, searchable data catalog and dictionary that provides rich metadata, lineage, and documentation \- improving discoverability and self\-service analytics across the organization.
   

  

 Champion Data Quality at Scale \- Implement automated data validation, anomaly detection, and reconciliation frameworks that ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency across the entire data lifecycle.
   

  

 Secure \& Govern Sensitive Data \- Implement encryption, fine\-grained access controls, audit trails, and compliance frameworks to protect highly sensitive payments and fraud data.
   

  

 Monitor, Optimize, Repeat \- Build observability into everything , proactive alerting, pipeline performance tracking, SLA monitoring, and intelligent auto\-remediation to ensure five\-nines data reliability.

 The AWS Payments \& Fraud Prevention team protects AWS and its customers from fraud, abuse, and account compromise at global scale. **Description**
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is building a central pipeline of Software Development Engineer (SDE II) talent. This requisition supports hiring across all AWS SDE II positions, from fungible SDE roles to specialized engineering positions in areas including:
  
  

* Embedded Systems
* Game Development
* Compiler Engineering
* Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning
* Healthcare AI
* Cloud Computing
* Distributed Systems
* Security Engineering
* Database Services
* Networking
* Analytics
* Infrastructure Services
* Firmware Development
* Video Processing and Streaming
* Content Delivery Network (CDN)

When you apply to this position, your profile will be considered for current and future SDE II openings across AWS
  
  
Key job responsibilities
  
  
**As An AWS Software Development Engineer, You Will**

* Design, develop, and maintain efficient, reusable, and reliable code
* Implement complex software solutions that meet business requirements
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define, design, and ship new features
* Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks and bugs
* Participate in architecture and design reviews to provide technical guidance
* Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities for process enhancement
* Stay current with emerging technologies and industry trends
* Mentor junior engineers and contribute to building a strong engineering culture

A day in the life
  
  
On a typical day as an AWS SDE, you might:
  
  

* Start your morning with a team stand-up to align on priorities and address any blockers
* Collaborate with product managers to refine requirements for upcoming features
* Write code and develop solutions for complex technical challenges
* Review pull requests from team members, providing constructive feedback
* Participate in design discussions for new services or features
* Debug and troubleshoot production issues as they arise
* Attend learning sessions to stay current with AWS technologies
* Document your work and contribute to technical specifications
* Engage with customers or internal stakeholders to better understand their needs

**About The Team**
Our central SDE sourcing team specializes exclusively in the SDE job family across AWS. This team of experts understands the nuances of various SDE roles throughout the organization and serves as your dedicated resource throughout the hiring process. Here's what you can expect:
  
  

* An SDE sourcer will contact you for an initial screening call to understand your background, skills, and interests
* They will share specific details about what you need to succeed in the interview process
* As the right roles become available, your sourcer will stay in touch and connect you with appropriate teams
* Throughout the process, the central team will provide guidance and preparation support

**Basic Qualifications**

* 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
* 3+ years of building production software experience
* 3+ years of building complex software systems experience
* 3+ years of contributing to new and current systems architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) experience
* Bachelor's degree or equivalent

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing
* Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence
* Knowledge of Python and/or C++ programming

At WEX, a Software Development Engineer (SDE) Level 3 is a senior technical leader who designs complete services, solves complex integration problems, and drives the lifecycle of major initiatives from end to end.
  
  
In this role, you will directly participate in WEX’s fast-paced AI-driven opportunities, acting as a key builder and strategist for next-generation technology. You will champion internal AI adoption by helping build AI-powered sofrware (using tools such as Google Gemini, AWS Agent Core, Claude, and other third-party agentic integrations) while sharing education and coaching within the organization.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**
**AI & Agentic Engineering**

* Agentic Workflows: Design and deploy multi-agent workflows within AWS Agent Core, effectively handling state management, memory persistence, and complex tool interactions.
* AI Leadership & Enablement: Help drive internal education and coaching initiatives for tools with as Google Gemini Enterprise; collaborate with external AI partners on new agentic opportunities.

**Architecture & System Design**

* End-to-End Ownership: Design, build, and own the lifecycle of entire services and cross-platform integrations. Solve complex system gaps and drive overarching audit strategies.
* Strategic Data Orchestration: Make critical trade-off decisions on data orchestration (e.g., MCP/API, Agents/Skills) based on robust data and requirements.
* Resilient Design: Build systems that handle failure gracefully by implementing retries, circuit breakers, and fallbacks. Ensure all designs are testable and maintainable long-term.
* Security First: Review code for security flaws and ensure all services adhere strictly to WEX’s authentication standards (e.g., OAuth scopes).

**Cloud Infrastructure, Reliability & CI/CD**

* Cost-Aware Cloud Architecture: Design reliable cloud infrastructure (e.g., auto-scaling groups, failover strategies) while proactively avoiding resource over-provisioning.
* Deployment & Environment Management: Own the automated deployment package and metadata framework. Write scripts or automation manifests to deploy configurations cleanly across sandbox tiers, preventing environment drift.
* CI/CD Optimization: Build and optimize CI/CD pipelines, focusing heavily on reducing build times and tightening feedback loops.
* Root Cause Resolution: Capable of solving complex bugs (intermittent issues, race conditions, memory leaks), ensuring the root cause is fixed permanently.
* Incident & Operations Leadership: Own Incidents for your services during outages. Create step-by-step triage runbooks and playbooks that empower Tier 1/2 helpdesk teams or junior analysts to resolve common platform errors without escalation.

**Product Partnership & Technical Leadership**

* Requirement Definition: Partner with Product Managers who define Functional requirements by owning the Non-Functional requirements (Performance, Security, Scalability) needed to meet business KPIs.
* Backlog & Scope Negotiation: Work with PMs to prioritize the backlog, explicitly negotiating the inclusion of "Tech Debt" and "Refactoring" by explaining long-term business risks. Negotiate "Must Haves" vs. "Nice to Haves" to ensure sprint achievability.
* Solution-Oriented Mindset: You don't say "No"; you say "Not like that." You offer alternative solutions that respect time and budget constraints.
* Empathic Mentorship & Review: Enforce strict quality standards during code reviews with empathy ("Check tone"). Reject sloppy or brittle "quick fixes" while setting the organizational standard for clean design patterns. Proactively mentor SDE 1s and 2s, delegating work specifically to help them grow.
* Consensus Building: Facilitate data-driven discussions to resolve engineering disagreements, effectively de-escalating "religious wars" about technology and ensuring "quiet" voices are heard in design meetings.
* Continuous Learning: Rapidly learn and apply new languages or frameworks, lead knowledge-sharing sessions, seek out critical feedback, and context-switch effectively across workstreams when project parameters change.

**Description**
 Do you want to build the infrastructure that every AWS service depends on before it can start? The AWS Secrets Management team builds and operates the system that distributes credentials and certificates to AWS's internal service fleet. The system sits on the critical path for service startup, runs across every host in the fleet, and has zero tolerance for downtime. As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will design and deliver backend services, APIs, and the host agent that powers credential distribution at massive scale. You will also lead migrations that modernize how credentials are stored and delivered, build AI\-agent\-driven operational tooling, and help bring the system up in new AWS regions. If you are a self\-starter who thrives on solving hard distributed\-systems problems with real, immediate impact, this is the role for you.
   

  

 Key job responsibilities
   

  

* Design and implement production backend services, APIs, and host\-level agents in Java, Rust, C\+\+, and Python that distribute credentials and certificates across AWS's internal fleet with high availability and zero downtime.
* Own end\-to\-end migrations of live, heavily depended\-upon systems, preserving backwards compatibility while modernizing how credentials are stored and delivered.
* Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, automated test coverage, and AI\-assisted operational tooling — including agentic coding tools for triage and remediation — to keep a fleet\-wide system operable at scale.
* Collaborate with security partner teams, product managers, and principal engineers on cross\-team designs, participating in written design reviews and code reviews to ensure solutions meet security and reliability requirements.
* Drive operational excellence through metrics, alarms, incident response, and on\-call rotations, identifying root causes and implementing permanent fixes to reduce operational burden over time.


 A day in the life
   

  

 Most of your time is heads\-down: writing code, reviewing designs, and working through complex migration plans for systems that thousands of other services depend on. Collaboration is concentrated at key moments — design reviews where you present your approach, code reviews where you give and receive candid feedback, and incident response where your deep knowledge of the system makes you the person others turn to. You use AI\-assisted engineering tools daily, both for coding and for operational triage, applying your judgment on when to trust their output.
   

  

**About The Team**
 The AWS Secrets Management team is responsible for credential and certificate distribution across AWS's internal service fleet. Our system is a dependency for a large number of AWS and Amazon services, which means the work we do is upstream of other teams' launches, migrations, and security commitments. We operate in an inclusive environment that values knowledge sharing and mentorship. Engineers each own an area of the system outright — serving as the required reviewer, the go\-to person during incidents, and the one who sets its technical direction. PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
  
  
Patient Care:
  
  
  

* Performs vascular access evaluation pre-treatment.

* Evaluates intradialytic problems and provides intervention as prescribed by physician order or as directed.
* Monitors patients’ response to dialysis therapy.

* Evaluates the patient prior to discharge.
* Documents information related to patient treatment include documentation in the patient health record.

* Enters all treatment data into the designated clinical application accurately and in a timely manner.

* Annual employer contribution to a health savings account.
* Generous paid time off varying by role and tenure in addition to 10 company-paid holidays.
* Market-leading retirement plan including a company match on employee 401(k) contributions, with a potential discretionary contribution based on company performance (no vesting period).
* Up to 12 weeks of paid parental time off (eligibility requires 12 months of continuous service with Cambia immediately preceding leave).
* Award-winning wellness programs that reward you for participation.
* Employee Assistance Fund for those in need.
* Commute and parking benefits.

We are happy to offer work from home options for most of our roles. To take advantage of this flexible option, we require employees to have a wired internet connection that is not satellite or cellular and internet service with a minimum upload speed of 5Mb and a minimum download speed of 10 Mb.
  
  
As part of our security requirements, new hires will need access to a personal mobile device to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) upon joining the company. MFA is an important layer of protection for accessing Cambia systems and is required for all employees.
